name: DHC-3 Otter
variants: Turbine conversions (Polar PT6A, Vazar, Texas Turbine)
summary: Large single-engine bush plane, the bigger sibling of the Beaver, usually seen on floats or tundra tires.

wings: High wing braced by a single strut on each side
Large, wide, constant-chord wing with big flaps
engines: Large radial engine in a round cowling (turbine conversions have a longer, narrower nose)
fuselage: Large, boxy, slab-sided fuselage with several large cabin windows
Large cargo-style doors; often on floats or skis

tellTales: Very large high-wing single with a round radial nose and a strut each side
Big, boxy fuselage with a tall angular tail, often on floats

confusedWith.howToTell: The Beaver is smaller, with a two-blade prop and fewer cabin windows; the Otter is a bigger aircraft with a three-blade prop.
The Caravan has tricycle gear and a turboprop nose; the Otter has a round radial nose and a tailwheel or floats.
The Kodiak has a turboprop nose, tricycle gear and a more modern shape; the Otter has a round radial nose and a boxy, 1950s fuselage.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
